ai.description: This toad reaches 7.5 cm. It is stout with a rounded body, dark brown skin, and broad, cream-colored lateral bands. Key features include a small, pointed head and short, powerful limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Kaloula pulchra* is best distinguished by the broad, distinct cream-to-yellowish bands running along its dark brown flanks, which are absent in similar Indian microhylids.
ai.habitat: *Kaloula pulchra* inhabits moist deciduous forests and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at low to moderate elevations near human settlements.
ai.behavior: When threatened, the Malaysian Narrowmouth Toad inflates its body like a balloon and secretes a sticky, white mucus to deter potential predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Kaloula pulchra* is an explosive breeder that lays eggs in temporary rain pools. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with females producing large clutches of eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Malaysian Narrowmouth Toad occurs in Northeast India, primarily in Assam and West Bengal, inhabiting low-elevation tropical forests and human-altered landscapes.
ai.callDescription: The Malaysian Narrowmouth Toad emits a loud, low-pitched, and resonant "ooh-ooh" call, often heard emanating from shallow, rain-filled pools during the monsoon season.
